title: The Irrationality of $e$ and $π$
summary: Unlike an ordinary fraction with an infinite numerator and denominator, an infinite continued fraction must be irrational. Euler was the first to show that the base of the natural logarithm $e$ is irrational, by numerically estimating its continued fraction, and showing the infinite sequence of convergents $p_n/q_n$ so obtained converged to $e$ using the Ricatti equation. Hermite showed that the recurrence relations for these convergents correspond to the recurrence relations between certain improper integrals, so proving the continued fraction tends to $e$ in the limit of infinite $n$.
